newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere end week down after GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: Solidere end week down after GDR issue.

text.p: Solidere shares fell on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on increased turnover in the week ended on Friday after the company made a $77-million issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs).
A shares fell to $113.375 from $114.75 last Friday and B shares closed at $117, down from $117.625.
On Monday, A shares closed at $115 while B shares reached $117.875. Both shares gradually fell to $113.625 and $117 respectively on Thursday, one day after the GDR issue was made.
"There were daily blocs of demand determining prices on the second fixing for the past few weeks. The objective was to maintain attractive prices ahead of the GDR issue," a dealer said.

The GDRs, each of which nominally represents one-tenth of an A share, were last quoted at $11.6 on the London Stock Exchange Automated Quotation system (SEAQ). They allow non-Arabs access to the market in Solidere for the first time.
Turnover rose sharply to 76,376 shares from last week's 45,354 and value was $8,447,309 from $5,206,291.
"Blocs of demand were met by increased supply hence boosting turnover for the week," a dealer said.
Also traded on the BSE during the week were 100 shares of Ciments Libanais at $1.25, down from $1.2812.
There was no trade in the three other listed companies: Eternit, Ciments Blancs, and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.6 percent on the week to 83.45 and the BLOM stock index also fell 1.09 percent to 971.74.
